take: Fyfe Golf makes headcovers to order in a workshop in Fife, out of Harris Tweed, Scottish tartan, waxed canvas from Dundee and, several times a year, something that used to be a completely different object — an RAF flight suit, a caddie’s coverall from Augusta, a deck chair, a bolt of sail cloth off a yacht on the west coast. Thirty-two pieces are below, twenty-three of them headcovers, all in stock on 14 September 2026.
story_extra: The brand started with a complaint. Neil Rennie had spent years walking into Scottish pro shops and finding nothing in them that had anything to do with Scotland. “Going around the pro shops and golf retailers, I couldn’t find that more elevated product, with heritage and provenance,” he told The Wandering Golfers in 2022. “Everything was mass-produced and heavily branded.” He had come out of fashion rather than golf, which meant he already knew who still wove cloth in Scotland and how to reach them. Fyfe launched in November 2021.

If you want the short version: the Harris Tweed covers are the reason to know the brand, the tartans are the ones people ask about, and the reclaimed-material projects are where it gets interesting — and where almost everything sells out inside a week.
